entertainment.summary: Drake also extends his record with 18 diamond plaques.
entertainment.body:
The diamonds keep on dancing on Drake . Ahead of The Boy’s 40th birthday this weekend, Drizzy earned 30 new certifications from the Recording Industry Association of America on Friday (Oct. 23).

Leading the pack are diamond certifications for VIEWS , “In My Feelings” and “Marvin’s Room,” while “God’s Plan” is now double-diamond.

As far as projects and albums go, Drake picked up certifications for More Life (6x), Certified Lover Boy (5x), Scorpion (9x), Care Package (1x), So Far Gone (3x) and ICEMAN is now platinum five months after its May arrival.

Singles earning certifications include: “Knife Talk” (8x), “First Person Shooter” (2x), “IDGAF” (2x), “You Broke My Heart” (1x), “Way 2 Sexy” (4x), “Girls Want Girls” (3x), “No Friends in the Industry” (3x), “Yebba’s Heartbreak” (2x), “Champagne Poetry” (2x), “Love All” (1x), “BACKOUTSIDEBOYZ” (1x), “Jumbotron Shit Poppin” (1x), “One Dance” (15x), “Fair Trade” (5x), “On BS” (2x), “Circo Loco” (1x), “Major Distribution” (1x), “Pussy and Millions” (1x), “Broke Boys” (1x) and “Privileged Rappers” (1x).

Drake is the first artist to surpass 350 million RIAA -certified units and is the most certified artist of all time. He also extends his record with 18 diamond plaques, which is the highest amount of any artist.

With all the new plaques on the way, Drizzy’s going to need another trophy room. The 6 God has plenty to celebrate this weekend, as Drake will be turning 40 on Saturday (Oct. 24).

entertainment.summary: The 28-year-old pop star gathered performers across two nights for the special event, which she closed out 70-minute headlining set.
entertainment.body:
Chappell Roan gathered together a slew of artists including Caroline Polachek, MUNA and surprise guest PinkPantheress in Los Angeles Thursday night for the second of two nights of The Super Graphic Spectacular.

The two-day event, held at the Shrine Auditorium and Expo Hall, was billed as a fundraising event featuring live performances, volunteer opportunities, connection and a special headlining set from Roan herself. Roan was preceded by sets from Polachek, Muna, Alisa Mae, Fantasia Royale Gaga and Sweat Eddie. With a block party that kicked off in the afternoon, the event, which raised money for the pop star’s foundation The Midwest Princess Project, which supports trans youth and the LGBTQ+ community. All proceeds of the event were donated to the organization. Related Stories Movies Tanner Buchanan, Peyton Elizabeth Lee to Star in 'Gasoline' From 'SLC Punk!' Director James Merendino (Exclusive) Music Victoria Justice on Releasing a Remixed "Love Zombie," a Viral Hit 15 Years in the Making

Comedian Caleb Hearon hosted the evening, and even joined MUNA during the band’s set. Roan delivered a high-energy performance to the just over 6,000 capacity room. It was a large underplay for the Rise and Fall of a Midwest Princess singer, who is without-a-doubt a stadium act at this point, having drawn an estimated 40,000 per night at her Pasadena shows last year. The audience for Thursday’s show was just as high-energy back, and an argument could be made that they might be one of the most engaged crowd’s the venue’s ever seen.

Roan used every inch of the gothic-themed stage during her roughly 70-minute set, kicking off with, unsurprisingly, “Super Graphic Ultra Modern Girl.” The setlist was consistent with other shows the singer’s done over the past year, leaning heavily on her breakout album The Rise and Fall of a Midwest Princess, with some newer songs — “The Subway,” “Good Luck, Babe!” and “The Giver” — sprinkled in.

During night one, Christina Aguilera joined Roan, and she sang her her classic hit “Beautiful” before the two singers joined together for a duet of “Coffee.” For night two, Roan mixed things up, bringing out PinkPantheress, describing the British pop star as being “fantastic” and “just so cunt” as she introduced her. Later in the show, Roan brought out Lola Young, who performed in one of the opening slots on night one, for a duet of Roan’s “Picture You.” The song, one of Roan’s more underrated offerings, was a highlight of the night.

entertainment.title: TV Ratings: ‘Cupertino’ and ‘Line of Fire’ More than Double in Delayed Viewing
entertainment.summary: Fellow first-year shows 'NCIS: New York' and 'Eternally Yours' also post sizable gains.
entertainment.body:
Logo text Cupertino and Line of Fire are very different shows on screen, but their ratings profiles early in the season are very similar.

Both shows draw about 3 million viewers for their initial airings (3.03 million for Cupertino’ s first two episodes on CBS, 2.98 million over three for Line of Fire on NBC). That’s not bad for a 10 p.m. network show — it tends to be the least watched hour of primetime — but a few other series that air in that hour are ahead of them.

Cupertino and Line of Fire are also picking up a lot of viewing — most of their seven-day totals, in fact — after those initial airings. The 2026-27 TV season is just a month old, so these are necessarily small sample sizes. But if these early patterns hold up, Cupertino and Line of Fire are poised to draw audiences well above their same-day audiences. Related Stories TV Streaming Ratings: 'Carrie' Has a Bloody Good Opening Week TV NBC Extends 'Line of Fire' With Full-Season Pickup

CBS’ two other rookies, NCIS: New York and Eternally Yours , also had good starts, with the former’s Oct. 6 series premiere ranking sixth among all network shows (excluding live sports) after a week of cross-platform viewing. The latest entry in the NCIS franchise grew to 10.25 million viewers over a week, according to Nielsen’s multi-platform ratings. That’s up from 5.62 million same-day viewers — a growth of 82 percent.

Of the 4.63 million additional viewers for NCIS: New York , 2.45 million came via streaming (about 24 percent of the all-in, seven-day total) and 2.18 million via DVR.

Cupertino’ s Oct. 8 premiere more than doubled after a week, going from 3.19 million on-air viewers to 7.17 million. The majority (2.18 million) of its after-air viewers came to the show via DVR, while an additional 1.8 million streamed the premiere in seven days.

Through its first three episodes, Line of Fire is averaging 6.9 million cross-platform viewers over a week, also more than doubling its initial audience (2.98 million). Its delayed viewing also tilts a little toward DVR playback (2.08 million viewers) vs. streaming (1.84 million). In announcing a full-season order for the show on Thursday, NBC also noted that the Sept. 21 premiere has grown to 14 million viewers over a month’s time.

Eternally Yours , a comedy about a family of vampires, also debuted Oct. 8. It had 4.12 million same-day viewers and 6.94 million after seven days, up 68 percent. About 1.58 million of those were streaming viewers, with 1.24 million coming from DVR playback.

She’s now becoming known for recording music in collaboration with the films she stars in, dropping “Dangerous” for Sinners in April of last year. “Blending music and acting like this feels like the fullest expression of who I am,” she told Billboard at the time.

entertainment.title: Vince Gill & Charlie Handsome Lead 2026 NMPA Gold & Platinum Gala Honorees
entertainment.summary: The 2026 National Music Publishers' Association Gold & Platinum Gala, held Thursday, honored over 150 Nashville songwriters.
entertainment.body:
The National Music Publishers’ Association celebrated an array of top country songs and the writers who created them Thursday night (Oct. 22), during the 8th annual NMPA Gold and Platinum Gala, held at the Country Music Hall of Fame and Museum in downtown Nashville.

The NMPA’s president/CEO David Israelite welcomed the audience of songwriters, music publishers and others in Nashville’s music industry elite, while the company’s Cara Cunningham and Charlotte Sellmyer were among those also leading the charge in honoring writers. Related Drake Becomes First Act to Surpass 350 Million RIAA-Certified Units, With 30 New Certifications Michael Saponara

The event honored over 150 songwriters whose country songs have achieved Gold, Platinum, Multi-Platinum and Diamond or above status, as certified by the Recording Industry Association of America (RIAA) from the July 2025-June 2026 eligibility period. Songwriting plaques were presented to more than 80 multi-platinum hitmakers from the Nashville community.

Recording Industry Association of America (RIAA) CEO Mitch Glazier was also in attendance to honor the hits and songwriters recognized during the ceremony.

Laci Kaye Booth launched the evening with a performance of her song “Daddy’s Mugshot,” featured on her new album Love Ain’t for the Faint of Heart .

The annual NMPA Gold and Platinum Gala honors new RIAA certifications for songs, no matter when they were initially released; thus, the evening feted songs both new and classic. Numerous songs were honored during the evening, including the Morgan Wallen-recorded “Chasing You,” which was celebrated Diamond, the Carrie Underwood-recorded “Before He Cheats” (11x Platinum), and a handful of 12x-Platinum songs: Shaboozey’s “A Bar Song (Tipsy),” Combs’s “Hurricane” and Wallen’s “Last Night,” as well as his 13x-Platinum “Whiskey Glasses.”

Also among the songs honored this year was the 3x Platinum “Jesus, Take the Wheel,” written by Gordie Sampson, Hillary Lindsey, and the late Brett James. Cornman Music president Nate Lowery accepted the accolade on behalf of James, who passed away just over a year ago. The audience responded with tremendous applause and a standing ovation.

The platinum anthem honor, which recognizes the highest-certified song of the year, went to “Beautiful Crazy,” written by Luke Combs, Rob Williford and Wyatt Durrette, and recorded by Combs. The song earned 15x Platinum certification in December 2025. Brett Young honored the writers by putting his own soulful spin on a performance of “Beautiful Crazy,” while songwriter Williford took the stage to accept the honor.

The end of the 2026 MLB Playoffs come down to two teams in the World Series , the American League champions Tampa Bay Rays and National League champions Milwaukee Brewers. Both teams are competing for their first-ever Commissioner’s Trophy, so the series is going to be one for the history books no matter which team wins. In 2026, the Tampa Bay Rays (98-64) takes on the Milwaukee Brewers (103-59) with Game 1 at American Family Field in Milwaukee, Wisconsin. The Brewers have home field advantage throughout the series. Tampa Bay Rays vs. Milwaukee Brewers broadcasts on starting Friday (Oct. 23) with first pitch at 8 p.m. ET/5 p.m. PT. The MLB championship series airs live on FOX.

The World Series is known for celebrity sightings, so it’s likely there may be a number of famous actors, actresses and recording artists in attendance for games in Milwaukee and Florida. Artists have been known to appear at games in the past, include Rays fans John Cena, Brittany Snow, Eric Church and others; Brewers fans Tom Brady, Stephen Colbert, Eric Benét and others.

For cord-cutters, there are a few ways to watch the World Series, if you don’t have cable, especially if you want to watch for free. DirecTV has a five-day free trial , while other streaming services, such as Fubo and Hulu + Live TV , offer free trials, so you can watch for free.

Sling TV offers the Blue plan, which comes with FOX for the Tampa Bay-Milwaukee series. With more than 40 channels, the streaming plan goes for $54.99 per month. The plan includes access to FOX One, while all plans come with a free cloud DVR and an extra 600 or so free channels too. Please note: Pricing and channel availability vary from market-to-market.

The broadcast network FOX for the Tampa Bay-Milwaukee series is available to watch with Hulu + Live TV . Prices for the cable alternative start at $49.99 for the first month ($99.99 per month afterward) for more than 100 live channels, while each plan comes with Hulu, Disney+ and ESPN Select at no additional cost. Hulu + Live TV might be best for those who want all of these streaming services together in one package.
